headline: US GOLDMINING LAUNCHES WHISTLER 2026 DRILL — $4.9B NPV AT SPOT, 8-10 PORPHYRY TARGETS IN 7.5×4.5KM CLUSTER, ALASKA (NASDAQ:USGO)
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (NASDAQ:USGO) announced July 6, 2026 commencement of its 2026 exploration drilling program at the 100%-owned Whistler Gold-Copper Project in Alaska — a 6,000-metre+ program targeting 8–10 high-priority geophysical and geological targets across a 7.5 × 4.5 kilometre porphyry cluster, with the program designed to test multiple systems identified by the 2025 airborne geophysical and surface geochemistry campaigns. Whistler hosts a PEA-level resource with a base-case NPV of approximately $2 billion that extends to $4.9 billion at current gold and copper spot prices ($4,183/oz gold, $6.17/lb copper) using the project's gold-copper co-product model. The project is in Alaska's prolific Yentna-Kahiltna district and is unencumbered — 100% owned with no joint venture partner dilution. For retail junior mining investors following U.S.-jurisdiction gold-copper development, the start of drilling marks the transition from evaluation to active exploration on one of the largest fully owned gold-copper porphyry targets on the NASDAQ, with 8–10 distinct targets providing a multi-hit catalyst window across the H2 2026 drilling season.

headline: GOLD $4,155 AND SILVER $62.77 ENTER KEY WEEK — FOMC MINUTES JULY 8 AND JOBS DATA AS NEXT MACRO TRIGGERS AFTER NFP MISS
snippet: Gold opened the week of July 7 at $4,155/oz and silver at $62.77/oz as markets entered what analysts identify as the first decisive macro catalyst week of H2 2026. The prior week's June NFP miss — 57,000 jobs versus 110,000 consensus — collapsed September Fed rate hike probability and delivered gold its first weekly gain in five consecutive weeks (+2.25%) and silver a 6.22% surge. The FOMC meeting minutes from the June 17 session, releasing July 8, are the primary near-term catalyst: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting statement removed forward guidance language and shifted the median dot to imply a single 25-basis-point hike, but the minutes will reveal whether the committee is hawkishly unified or split — a dovish split would be structurally gold-positive. Initial jobless claims (Thursday) and any Fed speaker commentary through the week complete the data calendar. For investors who entered gold at or near the June 24 low of $3,993, the week establishes whether the corrective base is holding and whether institutional re-accumulation above $4,100 can extend toward the primary $4,460 resistance level identified by multiple technical analysts.

headline: SILVER SURGES 6.22% AS NFP MISS ENDS GOLD'S 5-WEEK LOSING STREAK — RATE HIKE BETS COLLAPSE ON 57,000-JOB JUNE PAYROLL
snippet: Gold and silver posted their strongest weekly performances since February during the week ending July 3, 2026, driven entirely by the June non-farm payrolls miss: 57,000 jobs versus 110,000 consensus expectations, the weakest monthly print since March 2024. Gold rose 2.25% on the week to close at $4,183, snapping a five-week consecutive losing streak that had taken the metal from $5,405 (January 28 peak) to a $3,993 June 24 low. Silver's move was more emphatic — a 6.22% weekly surge to $62.36 — as the weaker employment data caused futures markets to slash September Fed hike probability, restoring silver's dual status as monetary metal and industrial commodity. The NFP report also showed downward revisions of 31,000 to April and May figures. September CME Fed funds futures probability for a 25bp hike fell from approximately 68% pre-NFP to under 35% post-release. CNBC analysis notes that the gold-silver ratio, which had widened significantly during the Q2 correction, compressed sharply — a pattern that historically precedes sustained precious metals outperformance in the 3–6 month window following major corrections.

headline: CATL RESTARTS JIANXIAWO: 100,000T/YR LITHIUM MINE BACK ONLINE — 3% OF GLOBAL SUPPLY RETURNS TO MARKET AFTER 18-MONTH SUSPENSION
snippet: CATL officially restarted operations at its Jianxiawo lithium mine in Jiangxi province on June 29, 2026, ending an 18-month voluntary suspension that the company had undertaken to support price stabilisation during the 2024–2025 lithium bear market. At 100,000 tonnes per year of lithium carbonate equivalent capacity, Jianxiawo represents approximately 8–10% of China's total domestic lithium production and roughly 3% of global supply — making its restart a material supply event. Battery-grade lithium carbonate in China had recovered to approximately 165,250 CNY/tonne from sub-50,000 CNY/tonne lows before the restart announcement; the return of this volume is expected to add an incremental 45,000+ tonnes of LCE supply in H2 2026. The restart was previously reported as 'possible' but has now been confirmed by multiple sources. For lithium junior investors, the return of Jianxiawo supply is a headwind against further near-term price appreciation in battery-grade carbonate — the market had priced in continued supply discipline from CATL, and the timing (concurrent with slowing EV sales globally) removes a key pillar of the 2026 lithium bull thesis. Western hard-rock producers with off-take agreements are less immediately affected than spot-exposed operators.

headline: ORETERRA METALS MOBILIZES TO BC GOLDEN TRIANGLE — $9.7M RAISED, 10,000M MAIDEN DRILL AT TREK SOUTH ADJACENT TO GALORE CREEK (TSXV:OTMC)
snippet: Oreterra Metals Corp. (TSXV:OTMC) announced July 3, 2026 mobilization of geological staff to its Trek South Copper-Gold Project in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, with camp establishment targeted for July 16 and a 10,000-metre maiden drill program to follow. The project is adjacent to the Galore Creek copper-gold porphyry — one of the largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits in North America, controlled by Newmont and Teck Resources — placing Trek South within a geological district that has attracted sustained major-company attention. Oreterra completed a $9.7 million oversubscribed private placement to fund the program, demonstrating institutional demand for BC Golden Triangle copper-gold exposure at current copper ($6.17/lb) and gold ($4,183/oz) prices. The 10,000-metre program will test multiple geophysical and geochemical anomalies identified in 2025 reconnaissance work. For retail investors following copper-gold porphyry exploration in proven Canadian jurisdictions, Trek South's adjacency to Galore Creek, oversubscribed financing, and maiden drill start represent the combination of geological prospectivity, financial readiness, and near-term catalysts that typically drives junior re-ratings in the 60–90 day window following first results.

headline: MYRIAD URANIUM PHASE II DRILL UNDERWAY: 4,500M AT COPPER MOUNTAIN, WYOMING — LUCKY CLIFF TARGET FOLLOWS PHASE I ANOMALIES (CSE:M)
snippet: Myriad Uranium Corp. (CSE:M) announced July 2, 2026 commencement of its Phase II drilling program at the Copper Mountain Uranium Project in Wyoming, a 4,500+ metre program targeting the Lucky Cliff deposit and follow-up on anomalies identified during Phase I. Wyoming hosts the Powder River Basin, one of North America's most productive in-situ recovery (ISR) uranium districts, and Copper Mountain sits within the broader Gas Hills/Copper Mountain uranium district where historical production and exploration have delineated multiple economic deposits. Uranium spot was approximately $85.70/lb as of early July 2026, significantly above the $65–$70/lb development threshold for most Wyoming ISR projects — providing favorable economics for any resource delineation results. Phase I drilling at Copper Mountain had returned anomalous uranium mineralization that defined the Lucky Cliff target zone now being drill-tested in Phase II. For retail uranium investors, Wyoming ISR projects with active drilling at $85/lb spot represent the segment of the uranium junior universe with the clearest path from exploration to production — ISR operations carry significantly lower capital costs and permitting timelines than conventional hard-rock uranium mining.

headline: GOLD RESOURCE + GOLDGROUP MERGER APPROVED 96% — $GORO COMBINATION CLOSES JULY 17 TO CREATE MEXICAN GOLD-SILVER PRODUCER (NYSE:GORO)
snippet: Gold Resource Corporation (NYSE:GORO) shareholders voted to approve the merger with Goldgroup Mining Inc. with approximately 96% support on July 2, 2026, clearing the final major shareholder condition for a combination that creates an enlarged Mexican gold-silver producer. The transaction is expected to close on or about July 17, 2026, subject to remaining closing conditions. The combination brings together Gold Resource's Don David Gold Mine in Oaxaca — a high-grade underground operation producing gold, silver, copper, lead, and zinc — with Goldgroup's Cerro Colorado heap-leach operation in Sonora, creating a dual-asset Mexican producer with complementary mine types and geological exposure. The 96% approval rate — well above the typical 70–80% threshold for contested transactions — signals minimal shareholder resistance and a clean path to closing. For investors tracking mid-tier M&A consolidation in Mexican gold-silver, the GORO/Goldgroup combination follows the broader 2026 trend of under-capitalised single-asset producers merging to achieve operational and financial scale, with the July 17 closing date providing a near-term catalyst for the combined entity's re-rating.

headline: DRC COBALT QUOTA ERROR STRANDS $1.1B IN EXPORTS; U.S. COMMITS $17.5B NUCLEAR LOANS — CRITICAL MINERALS WEEKLY ROUND-UP
snippet: InvestorNews's July 5, 2026 Critical Minerals Report covers three material developments: (1) A clerical quota allocation error in the DRC's cobalt export licensing system has stranded approximately 20,000 tonnes of refined cobalt — worth roughly $1.1 billion — at processing facilities and ports, as mismatched quota numbers have prevented export clearance across multiple producers; the error is expected to be corrected within 30 days but has created a temporary supply disruption that has lifted cobalt spot. (2) The U.S. Department of Energy formalized $17.5 billion in loan guarantees for advanced nuclear reactor construction, supporting 10 reactor projects — the largest single nuclear financing commitment in U.S. history and a direct structural demand signal for uranium and related critical inputs. (3) The EU and Brazil signed a bilateral critical minerals supply chain agreement covering lithium, cobalt, nickel, and rare earths — the third major Western bilateral minerals agreement in 2026 following U.S.-Canada and U.S.-Australia frameworks. For investors tracking policy-driven critical minerals demand, the nuclear loan commitment is the most structurally significant: at $17.5B in government-backed financing, it de-risks a multi-decade uranium demand runway beyond spot-price speculation.

headline: GOLDSEEK: FED CHAIR WARSH'S WILL VS. ECONOMIC REALITY — DEBT CEILING, DOLLAR BUBBLE, AND WHY THE CORRECTION IS ENDING
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis published in early July 2026 examines the structural tension between Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's stated commitment to continued rate restraint — reinforced at the ECB Forum on Central Banking in Sintra (July 1) — and the economic arithmetic that constrains actual policy: a $36 trillion federal debt load where every 100 basis points of rate increase adds approximately $360 billion in annual interest service, a commercial real estate sector facing $2.1 trillion in loan maturities through 2027, and a June payroll print (57,000 jobs) that makes the September hike dot far harder to execute than the median projection implies. The analysis draws on Warsh's own pre-Fed writing (notably his 2012 dissent memos from the Bernanke era) to argue that his hawkish framing is deliberate credibility management rather than executable policy — and that the gap between the Fed's stated dot-plot and the path it can actually deliver is precisely the mispricing that drove gold's corrective base at $3,993. For retail investors navigating the Q2 correction, the piece provides a framework for why institutional buyers did not flee the gold market at $4,000 despite the hawkish Fed narrative: the constraint on actual policy tightening is structural, not rhetorical.

headline: MONEY METALS: CONTINENTAL DOLLAR LESSON FOR 2026 — CURRENCY DEBASEMENT CYCLE REPEATS AS $36T DEBT FORCES MONETISATION
snippet: Money Metals Exchange published a July 3, 2026 Independence Day-timed audio analysis drawing a direct parallel between the Continental Currency debasement of the American Revolution — the origin of the phrase 'not worth a Continental' — and the structural trajectory of modern U.S. dollar purchasing power under a $36 trillion federal debt burden. The analysis traces the 1775–1781 currency collapse: Congress issued $241 million in Continentals against essentially no tax base, producing a 1000:1 depreciation within six years. The parallel it draws for 2026: the mechanisms differ (monetisation via central bank balance sheet expansion rather than printing press), but the fiscal arithmetic — spending commitments that outrun revenue by structural margins — is analogous. Gold's 2026 correction from $5,405 to $3,993 is framed as a sentiment reset, not a structural reversal, within a dollar-debasement cycle that has no politically viable exit without gold serving its traditional role as the residual store of value when fiat confidence erodes. Published on the eve of July 4 — the same date in 1776 that the Continental Congress adopted the Declaration that implicitly made the Continental Currency the founding financial obligation of the new republic — the timing is deliberate editorial framing for Money Metals' historically literate retail gold investor audience.
